header: Date: 2025-03-24 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Partnerships), Rita Patel (OrbitWare Head of Alliances), Tom Nguyen (OrbitWare Partner AE), Lina Gomez (OrbitWare Sales Ops)
summary: Weekly partner co-sell/pipeline review. Reviewed four joint opportunities (Acme, Nova Health, Vertex FinServ, Zephyr Retail). Aligned on next steps: joint demo scheduling, pricing share, performance benchmark plan, and CRM updates. Discussed competitive positioning versus OpenAI/Anthropic and confirmed Redwood Dedicated and Optimize are key selling points for low-latency, cost-controlled deployments.
transcript: [00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Rita: Rita here, hi all, thanks.
[00:07] Tom: Tom — OrbitWare partner AE, hello.
[00:09] Lina: Lina, Sales Ops.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus from Partnerships at Redwood.
[00:13] Priya: Priya, SE — I'll be handling perf and benchmarks.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool, agenda — quick pipeline review, highlight blockers, agree owners. I'll start with Acme — Tom, can you give status?

[00:25] Tom: Yeah, Acme is green lighted internally but they're hung up on latency and also procurement wants a dedicated environment. They asked about VPC and KMS — I said Redwood Private is an option but need details.

[00:37] Jordan: Right, Redwood Private or Dedicated are the two options. For Acme they asked for isolation and longer retention, so Private with customer-managed KMS makes sense. Priya can speak to expected latency on our Dedicated pools vs Private?

[00:47] Priya: Sure — Dedicated GPUs will hit low 10s of ms token latencies for their typical prompt sizes; Private depends on their infra but we can tune kernels and quantization, and we can run a quick perf benchmark. Note: KV cache warmup matters a lot for their workflow, that was fuzzy in the RFP.
[01:05] Tom: Got it. Procurement also flagged SOC2 and audit logs — Marcus, can you share the security doc?
[01:12] Marcus: Yep I will send the security pack. We have SOC2 Type II and ISO notes, plus integration guides for SAML/SSO and KMS. I'll share link after the call.
[01:20] Rita: On the commercial side Acme wants a pilot for 3 months with 1M tokens per month, and wants price protection if we move them to Dedicated. Jordan, what's our typical pilot pricing?

[01:30] Jordan: We usually do usage-based with a small committed monthly for pilot, then convert to reserved capacity for Dedicated with an uplift discount. I'll send the pilot sizing template. We may offer a short term discount as a co-sell incentive — Marcus, ok to propose?
[01:41] Marcus: Yes, we have a co-sell discount band. I'll coordinate approvals once we have deal size numbers.
[01:50] Lina: Quick CRM note — I updated stage to Proposal for Acme and attached notes about KMS ask.
[01:55] Jordan: Awesome. Next Nova Health — this one has regulatory constraints, wants data residency in EU. Tom?

[02:02] Tom: Nova Health is most interested in Redwood Private on-prem or VPC in EU. They asked about audit logs and retention policies. They also want references — any existing healthcare deployments?

[02:12] Marcus: We have two healthcare customers on Private, I can loop them in for references but will need approval. Also we should position Redwood Optimize and batching configs to control costs for their high throughput use case.

[02:24] Priya: Technically we can set up a regional Private deployment and test latency; recommend a small pilot first to validate throughput and quality. For healthcare, encryption at rest with customer KMS is critical.
[02:35] Rita: Okay noted. Vertex FinServ next — Jordan?

[02:38] Jordan: Vertex is more price-sensitive, they care about unit economics, so our cost/performance story matters. We should propose Redwood Dedicated with quantized model variants to reduce cost. Priya — can we benchmark quantized model for their workload?

[02:49] Priya: Yes, but we need their prompt set and expected sequence lengths. If they give 200-300 sample prompts we can run a perf + quality regression check. Quantization reduces GPU memory but we need to measure any quality delta.
[03:02] Tom: I'll get the sample prompts and share them by Friday.
[03:06] Jordan: Zephyr Retail is early stage — interest in embeddings for search and reranking. Low risk. We can demo hosted API to them. Marcus, any co-marketing ideas?
[03:16] Marcus: We could offer a joint case study if they convert. Also suggest a co-branded demo template to speed conversations. I'll draft one.
[03:23] Rita: On blockers — main ones are procurement (Acme), regulatory (Nova), and lack of sample prompts for Vertex. Anything else?

[03:30] Tom: One ask from partners — they want clarity on who owns the demos and intro sequencing. OrbitWare prefers to lead initial intro, Redwood to follow up technical deep-dive. We need to formalize handoff steps.
[03:41] Jordan: That's fine. Proposal: OrbitWare to do AE intro, Redwood to own technical demo and benchmark. We'll put that into the playbook and a one-pager for each opportunity.
[03:50] Marcus: Agree — I'll create a co-sell playbook snippet and share the link. Also include the decision tree for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[03:58] Priya: Quick technical note — for Acme's latency ask, continuous batching could increase throughput but may add tail latency for single requests. We should capture their SLOs (p50/p95) so we tune infra accordingly.
[04:10] Lina: Acme specified p95 < 200ms in their initial doc, not sure if that's tokens or end-to-end. I'll follow up.
[04:15] Jordan: Good. Competitive angle — several accounts mentioned OpenAI or Anthropic as fallback. How do we position?
[04:22] Marcus: Emphasize predictable unit economics, VPC/Private options, and enterprise controls. For FinServ, highlight audit logs, KMS, and rollout policies.
[04:32] Tom: Partners also asked about a quick POC — do we have a standard POC checklist?
[04:37] Jordan: Yes, I'll share the pilot checklist. Priya will own perf tests and quality guardrails.
[04:42] Priya: For perf tests I need sample prompts, token distribution, and target concurrency. Also permission to store minimal logs for debugging during test.
[04:51] Tom: I'll collect the artifacts for Vertex and Acme and upload to the shared drive.
[04:55] Marcus: Logistics — marketing collateral, joint deck, and pricing sheet. I'll push the deck and one-pager after call. Jordan will attach pricing.
[05:03] Rita: Timing — if we can have the Acme pilot scoped next week we can close Q2. Everyone aligned?
[05:10] Jordan: Yes, target pilot kickoff first week of April. We'll aim to have benchmark plan and pricing by end of next week.
[05:16] Lina: I'll update CRM now and send calendar invites for demos once Tom confirms dates.
[05:20] Tom: Quick question — any special legal T&Cs partners should expect?
[05:24] Marcus: Standard enterprise MSA for Dedicated/Private, we can share a redline template. For pilots we use an MSA + SOW, I'll attach both.

[05:31] Jordan: Ok let's recap actions — Marcus to send co-sell deck and security docs; Jordan to send pricing and pilot template; Priya to draft benchmark plan; Tom to gather prompts and make intros; Lina to update CRM. Any other items?
[05:44] Rita: Nothing else from OrbitWare, thanks everyone.
[05:47] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up in Slack and email. Meeting adjourned.
